check: Scope of definition; marking requirement; oral/visual information; derivatives; Affiliates' information
preferred: Broad: all forms, no marking required, includes derivatives and Affiliates' information and anything reasonably considered confidential by its nature
fallback: Marking required, with oral/visual information confirmed in writing (with a summary) within 30 days
red_flag: Marking required with no written-confirmation route for oral information, or a confirmation period under 30 days; Affiliates' information excluded
sample_language: "Confidential Information" means all information relating to the Disclosing Party, its Affiliates or the Purpose, in any form and whether or not marked, including any information which by its nature would reasonably be considered confidential and all analyses and documents generated from it.
rationale: Marking every item is impractical in ongoing discussions; protection should follow the nature of the information rather than its labelling.

preferred: Marked as confidential; oral/visual information confirmed in writing with a summary within 30 days
fallback: Marked, or would reasonably be understood to be confidential
red_flag: Unlimited scope including derivatives, with no marking or reasonableness limit
sample_language: All Confidential Information shall be marked "Confidential" or, if disclosed orally or visually, confirmed in writing as confidential with a summary within thirty (30) days of disclosure.
rationale: A clear marking requirement gives both Parties certainty as to which information is protected.

preferred: Broad categories including derivatives and Affiliates' information; marked, or oral/visual information confirmed in writing within 30 days
fallback: Marked, or would reasonably be understood to be confidential
red_flag: Strict marking with no route for oral information, or broad scope with no exclusions
sample_language: ...shall be marked "Confidential" or, in the case of oral or visual disclosure, confirmed in writing as confidential within thirty (30) days.
rationale: This balances broad protection with certainty as to what is covered.

clause: Confidentiality of the Agreement and discussions
check: Whether the existence and content of the Agreement and the discussions are protected
preferred: Existence and content of the Agreement and discussions on the Purpose are Confidential Information
fallback: Content of the Agreement and discussions protected; existence may be disclosed
red_flag: Neither the content of the Agreement nor the discussions are protected
sample_language: "Confidential Information" includes the existence and content of this Agreement and discussions in relation to the Purpose.
rationale: Discussions about a potential transaction are commercially sensitive in themselves.

check: Which exclusions apply; burden of proof; combination (anti-aggregation) wording
preferred: Standard exclusions; burden of proof on Receiving Party; exclusions do not apply to specific information merely because it is embraced by, or combined with, excluded information
fallback: Standard exclusions; burden of proof on Receiving Party
red_flag: Exclusions broader than market standard; no burden of proof on Receiving Party
sample_language: The foregoing exceptions shall not apply to specific Confidential Information merely because it is embraced by more general information, or to any combination of information merely because individual elements fall within an exception.
rationale: Individually public elements can still be confidential when combined; the exclusions should not undermine that protection.

preferred: Public domain, prior possession or lawful third-party source, independent development, and disclosure with prior written consent
fallback: Standard exclusions, accepting combination wording and burden of proof
red_flag: Missing independent development or prior possession
sample_language: ...(c) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without reference to or reliance upon the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.
rationale: Standard exclusions protect each Party's legitimate pre-existing and independently developed information.

preferred: Standard exclusions; burden of proof on Receiving Party
fallback: Standard exclusions; burden of proof not specified
red_flag: Any standard exclusion missing
sample_language: In any dispute with respect to these exclusions, the burden of proof will be on the Receiving Party.
rationale: These are the market-standard exclusions for a mutual NDA.

check: Whether the Purpose is clearly defined; use limited to the Purpose; no use for own interest
preferred: Purpose specific to the transaction; no use for own interest or other purposes
fallback: Purpose defined at project level
red_flag: Broad Purpose (e.g. 'business relationship') or no Purpose stated
sample_language: In connection with the discussion, negotiation or collaboration between the Parties regarding [describe transaction] (the "Purpose")...
rationale: A defined Purpose is necessary to determine what use of the information is permitted.

check: Who may receive information; written confidentiality obligations; Receiving Party's liability; Affiliate involvement
preferred: Need-to-know Representatives under written confidentiality obligations; Affiliates only if bound by the Agreement; Receiving Party fully responsible for both
fallback: Affiliates and advisors permitted; Receiving Party remains liable
red_flag: Disclosure to lenders or third parties without consent; Receiving Party not liable for Representatives or Affiliates
sample_language: The Receiving Party shall be fully responsible for any non-compliance by its Representatives and Affiliates with this Agreement as if it were its own breach.
rationale: The Disclosing Party has no contractual relationship with the Representatives, so the Receiving Party should remain responsible for them.

preferred: Includes Affiliates, advisors, auditors and financiers without separate NDAs
fallback: Need-to-know Representatives of the Party and its Affiliates, under written confidentiality obligations
red_flag: Individual approval required; each Representative must sign an NDA directly with the Disclosing Party
sample_language: "Representatives" means directors, officers, employees, advisors and auditors of a Party or its Affiliates who need to know the Confidential Information for the Purpose.
rationale: Affiliates and professional advisors may need access to evaluate the Purpose.

preferred: Need-to-know Representatives of the Party and its Affiliates; written confidentiality obligations; Party responsible for their compliance
fallback: Affiliates excluded, but consent not to be unreasonably withheld
red_flag: No need-to-know requirement
sample_language: ...limit disclosure on a need-to-know basis to its Representatives who are under written obligations of confidentiality, and shall be responsible for their compliance.
rationale: This reflects the market-standard approach to Representatives.

preferred: Strict confidentiality: no disclosure, copying, reverse engineering or use outside the Purpose without prior written consent
fallback: Same as own, no less than reasonable care
red_flag: 'Same as own' with no minimum standard
sample_language: ...to keep all Confidential Information strictly confidential and not to copy, reverse engineer or use it except as necessary for the Purpose.
rationale: Clear prohibitions give the Disclosing Party certainty on how its information will be handled.

preferred: Reasonable care
fallback: Same as own, no less than reasonable care
red_flag: Highest degree of care or absolute standard
sample_language: ...with reasonable care to prevent unauthorised disclosure.
rationale: Reasonable care is the recognised market standard and is capable of objective assessment.

preferred: Same as own, no less than reasonable care
fallback: Strict confidentiality with express prohibitions
red_flag: Highest degree of care, or no minimum at all
sample_language: ...the same degree of care it uses for its own confidential information, but in no event less than reasonable care.
rationale: This is the market-standard formulation.

check: Whether security obligations apply and whose standards
preferred: Counterparty complies with our information-security policies and standards, as updated from time to time
fallback: Reasonable, industry-standard security measures
red_flag: No security obligations where sensitive or IT-related information is shared
sample_language: The Receiving Party shall comply with the Disclosing Party's information-security policies and standards as notified from time to time.
rationale: Security obligations must match the sensitivity of the information shared.

preferred: Reasonable, industry-standard security measures
fallback: Compliance with the other Party's policies as provided at signing
red_flag: Compliance with policies the other Party may change unilaterally without notice
sample_language: Each Party shall implement reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect the other Party's Confidential Information.
rationale: A Party cannot comply with standards that may change without notice.

preferred: Mutual obligation to apply reasonable technical and organisational security measures
fallback: Compliance with the other Party's policies provided in advance
red_flag: One-sided obligation, or policies changeable unilaterally
sample_language: Each Party shall implement reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect the other Party's Confidential Information.
rationale: Security obligations in a mutual NDA should apply equally.

check: Prior notice; cooperation; disclosure limited to what is required
preferred: Prior written notice; cooperation in testing the requirement or seeking a protective order; disclose only the portion required; provide the Disclosing Party a copy of what was disclosed
fallback: Notice to the extent legally permitted
red_flag: No notice required; unlimited disclosure
sample_language: ...give the Disclosing Party prior written notice, co-operate in seeking a protective order, disclose only the portion legally required and provide the Disclosing Party with a copy of the information disclosed.
rationale: Notice allows the Disclosing Party to protect its information through available legal means.

check: As above, plus stock exchange carve-out
preferred: Notice to the extent legally permitted; cooperation at Disclosing Party's cost; no notice for routine regulatory examinations
fallback: Notice where practicable; cooperation at Disclosing Party's cost
red_flag: Absolute prior notice even where legally prohibited; cooperation at own cost; no stock exchange carve-out
sample_language: ...including disclosure required by the rules of any stock exchange on which a Party or its Affiliate is listed.
rationale: A Party may be subject to mandatory disclosure obligations, such as stock exchange rules, that cannot be contractually restricted.

preferred: Notice to the extent legally permitted; reasonable cooperation at Disclosing Party's cost; disclose only what is required; stock exchange carve-out
fallback: Notice where practicable
red_flag: No notice at all, or unlimited cooperation at own cost
sample_language: ...at the Disclosing Party's expense, and disclose only the portion legally required.
rationale: This balances legal compliance with protection of the Disclosing Party.

check: Where a Party is listed, whether the counterparty undertakes not to trade on inside information
preferred: Counterparty acknowledges the listed Party's status and will not deal in its or its Affiliates' securities on the basis of non-public information
fallback: General undertaking to comply with applicable securities laws
red_flag: No securities-law undertaking where material non-public information about a listed Party is shared
sample_language: The Receiving Party shall not, and shall procure that its Representatives do not, deal in the securities of the Disclosing Party or its Affiliates while in possession of material non-public information.
rationale: Where a Party is listed, confidential information may constitute inside information under securities laws.

check: Compliance undertakings and whose code of conduct applies
preferred: Counterparty adheres to our code of conduct and complies with applicable laws
fallback: Mutual compliance with applicable laws
red_flag: We must adhere to the counterparty's code of conduct or internal policies
sample_language: Each Party shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations in connection with this Agreement.
rationale: Compliance obligations should be clear and based on applicable law.

preferred: Notify immediately; personal data within 24 hours; remediate and provide incident details
fallback: Personal data within 48 hours
red_flag: No notification obligation; personal data beyond 72 hours
sample_language: ...notify the Disclosing Party without undue delay and, for personal data, within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware.
rationale: Data controllers must notify the regulator within 72 hours under the PDPA and GDPR, so earlier notice is required to comply.

preferred: Without undue delay; personal data within 48-72 hours
fallback: 24 hours from confirmation of the incident (not mere suspicion)
red_flag: Every suspected event within a very short period; Disclosing Party right to access our systems
sample_language: ...within forty-eight (48) hours after confirming such incident.
rationale: Time is needed to verify an incident before notification so that information provided is accurate.

preferred: Without undue delay; personal data within 48 hours
fallback: 24 hours
red_flag: Personal data beyond 72 hours, or no timeframe
sample_language: ...without undue delay and, for personal data, within forty-eight (48) hours of becoming aware.
rationale: This allows verification while leaving time for regulatory notification.

check: Applicable laws; allocation of obligations; cross-border transfer
preferred: Strict compliance with all applicable privacy laws including the GDPR and the Thai PDPA; Receiving Party applies appropriate security
fallback: Compliance with applicable data protection laws generally
red_flag: Uncapped indemnity from Disclosing Party for personal data
sample_language: The Parties shall strictly comply with all applicable privacy laws, including the General Data Protection Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and the Thai Personal Data Protection Act B.E. 2562.
rationale: Where personal data is subject to both the PDPA and the GDPR, both regimes should be covered.

preferred: No personal data unless requested; Disclosing Party warrants lawful basis
fallback: Mutual compliance with PDPA and GDPR
red_flag: Receiving Party liable for Disclosing Party's deficiencies in collecting the data
sample_language: Neither Party shall disclose personal data unless requested. The Disclosing Party warrants it has a lawful basis for such disclosure.
rationale: Only the Disclosing Party can ensure a lawful basis exists at the point of collection.

preferred: Mutual strict compliance with applicable privacy laws including PDPA and GDPR; personal data obligations survive
fallback: PDPA only if no EU data involved
red_flag: No personal data provisions; cross-border transfer with no transfer mechanism
sample_language: The Parties shall strictly comply with all applicable privacy laws, including the GDPR and the Thai PDPA.
rationale: This reflects each Party's own statutory obligations.

preferred: Within 30 days of request or termination; certification of destruction; exceptions for legal requirements and back-up only; no recovery of back-up copies
fallback: Certification on request
red_flag: Broad 'internal policy' exception; no timeframe; no certification
sample_language: ...within thirty (30) days return or destroy all Confidential Information and certify such destruction. Retained back-up copies shall remain confidential and shall not be recovered.
rationale: A fixed timeframe and certification give the Disclosing Party assurance that its information is no longer in use.

preferred: As soon as practicable; retention permitted for legal, internal policy, back-up and legal record purposes
fallback: Exceptions for legal requirements and back-up only, with 30-day timeframe
red_flag: Deletion of back-ups required; director certification within a short period
sample_language: ...except as required by law, internal record-keeping policy or automatic IT back-up, which shall remain subject to this Agreement.
rationale: Deleting data from automated back-up systems is often technically impracticable; retained data remains protected.

preferred: Within 30 days; exceptions for law and back-up; certification; retained data remains confidential
fallback: As soon as practicable, certification on request
red_flag: No return or destruction obligation
sample_language: ...within thirty (30) days of request, return or destroy all Confidential Information and certify such destruction.
rationale: This is a practical, market-standard approach.

check: Liability cap; exclusion of indirect loss and its carve-outs
preferred: No cap; indirect loss excluded except for wilful misconduct, fraud, gross negligence and unauthorised use or disclosure of Confidential Information
fallback: No cap; indirect loss excluded except for wilful misconduct, fraud or gross negligence
red_flag: Low cap; exclusion of indirect loss including loss of profit with no carve-outs
sample_language: Neither Party shall be liable for indirect or consequential damages unless caused by the wilful misconduct, fraud or gross negligence of such Party or its Representatives, or by unauthorised use or disclosure of Confidential Information.
rationale: Loss from misuse of confidential information typically takes the form of lost profit; excluding it without carve-outs would leave no effective remedy.

preferred: Liability for proven direct loss only; indirect loss including loss of profit excluded
fallback: Indirect loss excluded except for wilful misconduct, fraud or gross negligence
red_flag: One-sided or uncapped indemnity including indirect loss
sample_language: No Party shall be liable for any indirect, special or consequential loss, including loss of profit.
rationale: Liability should be proportionate and limited to direct, proven loss.

preferred: Mutual; no cap; indirect loss excluded except for wilful misconduct, fraud or gross negligence
fallback: Mutual liability for direct loss only
red_flag: One-sided liability or indemnity
sample_language: Neither Party shall be liable for any indirect or consequential damages unless caused by the wilful misconduct, fraud or gross negligence of such Party or its Representatives.
rationale: Mutual obligations should carry mutual and proportionate liability.

check: Right to injunction; acknowledgement that damages are inadequate
preferred: Acknowledgement that damages are inadequate; Disclosing Party entitled to injunction or specific performance in addition to other remedies
fallback: Entitled to seek injunctive relief
red_flag: No injunctive relief provision
sample_language: ...monetary damages would not be an adequate remedy and the Disclosing Party shall be entitled to an injunction, specific performance or other equitable relief.
rationale: Damages alone cannot undo the disclosure of confidential information.

preferred: May seek, at the court's or tribunal's discretion
fallback: Mutual 'entitled to'
red_flag: Advance acknowledgement that damages are inadequate plus waiver of security/bond
sample_language: ...may seek injunctive relief as a court of competent jurisdiction may grant.
rationale: Equitable relief should remain subject to the court's assessment of the circumstances.

preferred: Either Party, as Disclosing Party, entitled to seek injunction or specific performance
fallback: Mutual, may seek
red_flag: One-sided
sample_language: Each Party may seek injunctive relief in addition to other remedies.
rationale: Remedies should be available equally to both Parties.

check: Any licence granted; restrictions on IP filings and reverse engineering
preferred: No rights granted; no IP filings based on Confidential Information; no reverse engineering
fallback: No rights granted
red_flag: Licence or feedback clause allowing free use of our input
sample_language: The Receiving Party shall not file any intellectual property application based upon, or reverse engineer, any Confidential Information.
rationale: An NDA is intended to protect information, not to transfer rights in it.

preferred: No press release or statement about the Confidential Information or the collaboration without consent, except as required by law or stock exchange rules
red_flag: No exception for disclosure required by law or stock exchange rules
sample_language: ...save as required by law or the rules of any stock exchange.
rationale: A Party may be subject to mandatory disclosure requirements.

check: Right to use information retained in memory
preferred: Delete
fallback: Limited to unaided memory; excludes trade secrets, personal data and patented information
red_flag: Broad residuals clause
sample_language: [Delete clause]
rationale: A residuals clause would effectively permit use of Confidential Information outside the Purpose.

preferred: Include residuals clause
fallback: Delete residuals, but retain freedom to conduct similar discussions and independent development
red_flag: Restriction on developing similar products or holding similar discussions
sample_language: This Agreement shall not limit either Party from conducting similar discussions or independently developing products without use of the other Party's Confidential Information.
rationale: Each Party must remain free to conduct its own independent business development.

preferred: No residuals; freedom to conduct similar discussions
fallback: Narrowly limited residuals
red_flag: Broad residuals or restriction on similar discussions
sample_language: This Agreement shall not limit either Party from conducting similar discussions, provided it does not breach this Agreement.
rationale: This protects confidential information without restricting legitimate business activity.

preferred: Not included in the NDA
fallback: 12 months, limited to employees involved in the Purpose, with general advertising carve-out
red_flag: More than 12 months or covering all group employees
sample_language: ...provided that general solicitations not targeted at such employees shall not breach this clause.
rationale: Non-solicitation is outside the scope of a confidentiality agreement and, if included, should be narrowly limited.

check: Agreement term; survival period after expiry; trade secrets and personal data
preferred: Agreement term plus 5-year survival after expiry or termination; trade secrets and personal data indefinitely
fallback: Agreement term plus 3-year survival
red_flag: Obligations end with the Agreement term, or survival under 2 years
sample_language: ...the Receiving Party shall continue to be bound by the obligations of confidentiality and non-use for five (5) years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement.
rationale: Confidential information remains sensitive after discussions end, so obligations should survive expiry.

preferred: Total obligation period of 2 years
fallback: Agreement term plus 2-year survival
red_flag: Indefinite (other than personal data) or survival over 5 years
sample_language: ...shall continue to be bound for two (2) years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement.
rationale: A defined period is needed to manage retention and compliance obligations.

preferred: Agreement term plus 3-year survival; trade secrets and personal data indefinitely
fallback: Agreement term plus 2-year survival for short-term transactions
red_flag: No survival after the Agreement term
sample_language: ...shall continue to be bound by the obligations of confidentiality and non-use for three (3) years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement.
rationale: Three years' survival is market standard for a mutual NDA.

check: Whether assignment is permitted; Affiliate carve-out; liability after assignment
preferred: No assignment without consent, except to an Affiliate; assignor and assignee jointly liable
fallback: Consent required in all cases, with joint and several liability
red_flag: Counterparty may assign freely on a one-sided basis
sample_language: ...save that either Party may assign this Agreement to its Affiliate upon written notice. The assigning Party and the assignee shall be jointly and severally liable for compliance with this Agreement.
rationale: Parties commonly reorganise activities between Affiliates, while the original Party should remain accountable.

check: Governing law; arbitration or courts; seat and language; injunction carve-out
preferred: Thai law; arbitration under the Thai Arbitration Institute rules in Bangkok, in English, 3 arbitrators; carve-out for urgent injunctive relief in any competent court
fallback: Singapore law; SIAC arbitration seated in Singapore; sole arbitrator for low-value matters
red_flag: Law or courts of the counterparty's home country; no carve-out for urgent injunctive relief
sample_language: ...finally resolved by arbitration under the rules of the Thai Arbitration Institute, seated in Bangkok and conducted in English. Nothing shall prevent either Party from seeking urgent injunctive relief from any competent court.
rationale: Arbitration provides a neutral forum and awards are enforceable internationally under the New York Convention.

check: Obligation to proceed; warranty of accuracy
preferred: No obligation to proceed; no representation or warranty on the information; only warranties in a definitive agreement have effect
red_flag: Disclosing Party warrants accuracy or completeness of information
sample_language: Only those representations or warranties made in a final definitive agreement concerning the Purpose will have legal effect.
rationale: Information is shared for evaluation only; any warranties belong in the definitive agreement.

preferred: Limited to this subject matter; does not affect existing agreements on other matters
red_flag: Broad supersession of all prior agreements between the Parties
sample_language: This Agreement comprises the entire agreement between the Parties concerning the subject matter hereof.
rationale: Existing agreements between the Parties should continue to apply to their own subject matter.

check: Whether we must communicate the counterparty's privacy notice to our personnel
preferred: Mutual, or delete
fallback: One-sided if the burden is minimal
red_flag: One-sided obligation for us to notify our directors/employees of the counterparty's privacy notice
sample_language: Each Party shall inform its personnel whose personal data is provided to the other Party of the other Party's privacy notice.
rationale: Obligations concerning personal data exchanged between the Parties should apply equally to both.
